Introduction to EcoWat  
Category: Overview
Related topics: Account, Dashboard  
What is EcoWat?  
EcoWat is an AI-based electricity and resource-saving platform designed for German electricity consumers. It makes household energy use smarter, cheaper, and greener by automating the timing of appliance use.  
EcoWat is built specifically for regions with dynamic (hourly-changing) electricity pricing and variable renewable energy generation, where the timing of appliance use has genuine financial and environmental value.  
Core Features  
EcoWat includes the following integrated features:  
Smart appliance scheduling that automatically times appliances to run when electricity is cheapest and cleanest
Ecky, an AI chatbot that answers energy-related questions and provides personalized suggestions
A personalized dashboard summarizing consumption, costs, and savings
Live electricity price and renewable-availability tracking with 7-day predictions
Who EcoWat is For  
EcoWat is designed for individual households and residents who:  
Pay for their own electricity
Want to reduce both energy costs and environmental footprint
Are not energy experts
Benefit from better visibility into consumption habits  
EcoWat is especially valuable in regions with variable or dynamic electricity pricing like Germany, but useful to anyone wanting better energy awareness.  
Design Principles  
EcoWat follows these core principles:  
Keep the interface approachable for non-technical users
Be transparent about where AI is used and how confident predictions are (via ML badges)
Default to suggestions that save both money and the environment simultaneously
Prioritize security and privacy of user data at every layer
Mission  
The broader mission of EcoWat is to help people build sustainable, schedule-aware habits around energy use. When many households adopt energy-conscious habits together, the cumulative impact on energy grids and the environment becomes significant.

Getting Started — Quick Guide  
Category: Getting Started
Related topics: Account, Dashboard, Appliances  
Setup Steps  
Follow these steps to set up EcoWat from scratch:  
1. Install or Open EcoWat
Desktop users: Use the website (no Windows or macOS desktop app exists)
Mobile users: Download the native app for Android or iOS  
Both the website and app provide identical full functionality.  
2. Create an Account  
Register with a unique email address and choose a password meeting these minimum requirements:  
At least 6 characters
At least 1 uppercase letter
At least 1 special character (such as !, @, #, $, or %)  
After submitting registration, check your inbox for a verification email and click the link to fully activate the account.  
3. Log In  
Sign in with your username and password, or use the passwordless Magic Link option by entering your email and clicking the link sent to your inbox.  
4. Explore the Dashboard  
The dashboard is your home base for EcoWat. It summarizes:  
Current and predicted electricity consumption
Live pricing
Renewable-energy availability
Personalized suggestions  
Because the account is new, predictions become more personalized over time as EcoWat learns from your actual usage.  
5. Add Your First Appliance  
Adding an appliance (such as a washing machine or dishwasher) along with its typical usage pattern lets EcoWat begin factoring it into scheduling suggestions.  
6. Try Asking Ecky  
Ask Ecky questions such as:  
"What's the cheapest time to run my washing machine today?"
"How does my usage this week compare to last week?"
7. Understand ML Badges  
Look for small ML badge icons on various dashboard features. These icons flag outputs generated by machine learning versus straightforward calculations.  
8. Manage Your Account  
Access the Profile page to:  
Update email or password
Review registered appliances
Delete your account

Carbon Footprint and Environmental Impact  
Category: Feature
Related topics: Renewability Score, Recommendations, Terminology  
Understanding Carbon Footprint  
Your household's carbon footprint is the total greenhouse gas emissions produced by generating the electricity you consume. Carbon footprint varies based on:  
Total consumption (kWh): The more electricity used, the higher the footprint
Energy source mix: Electricity generated from fossil fuels (coal, natural gas) creates higher emissions than renewable sources (wind, solar)
How EcoWat Calculates Environmental Impact  
EcoWat calculates environmental impact using Germany's current grid composition and renewable availability:  
When renewable generation is high (high renewability score), the grid relies less on fossil fuels, and consuming electricity during those hours creates lower emissions
When renewable generation is low, fossil-fuel plants contribute more to grid supply, and consuming electricity during those hours creates higher emissions
Renewability Score Connection  
The renewability score (0–100%) indicates how much of Germany's current grid generation comes from renewable sources (solar and wind). Higher scores correspond to lower carbon intensity.  
Benefits of Scheduling Around Renewables  
Running appliances during "green hours" (high renewable availability hours) provides multiple benefits:  
BenefitExplanation
Lower emissionsMore of your consumed electricity comes from clean sources
Environmental impactReduces reliance on fossil-fuel generation
Grid healthShifts demand away from coal/gas plants toward renewable sources
Sometimes cost savingsHigh-renewable hours often coincide with low-price hours
Household and Grid-Level Impact
Individual Household Impact  
Small, consistent changes add up significantly over time. Running a single appliance during green hours saves emissions, and this benefit compounds across days, weeks, and months.  
Collective Impact  
When many households shift consumption toward off-peak and renewable-rich hours, the cumulative effect:  
Reduces strain on fossil-fuel power plants
Lowers overall grid emissions
Encourages grid operators to prioritize renewable generation
Creates market incentives for additional renewable capacity
Tracking Your Environmental Impact  
EcoWat displays environmental benefits in recommendations, showing:  
Emissions avoided by following a recommendation
Fossil-fuel generation offset by shifting consumption to green hours
Total environmental impact of your scheduling choices

7-Day Consumption Forecast  
Category: Feature
Related topics: Dashboard, Terminology  
What is the 7-Day Forecast?  
The 7-day consumption forecast predicts your household's daily electricity consumption for each of the next 7 days. The forecast appears on the Dashboard and updates regularly as new data becomes available.  
How the Forecast Works  
EcoWat's consumption forecast model takes 31 input features to predict daily consumption:  
Household size
Weather temperature (current and forecast)
Day of week
Weekend flag
Yesterday's total electricity consumption (kWh)
7-day historical average consumption (kWh)
Planned operating hours for 19 different supported appliance types  
The model processes these inputs to generate a predicted kWh value for each of the next 7 days.  
ML Badge  
The 7-day forecast carries an ML badge, indicating it is powered by a machine learning model and carries some margin of error. The forecast is an informed suggestion, not a guaranteed prediction.  
Treat the forecast as a helpful guide for understanding your likely electricity usage trends, not as a precise fact.  
How to Use the Forecast  
Use the 7-day forecast to:  
Understand your typical weekly consumption patterns
Identify days when you expect higher usage
Plan when to run flexible appliances (like laundry) based on expected consumption
Track how well EcoWat's predictions align with your actual usage over time

Ecky — AI Assistant  
Category: Feature
Related topics: Dashboard, Appliances, Recommendations  
What is Ecky?  
Ecky is EcoWat's AI chatbot assistant. Ecky answers energy-related questions and provides personalized suggestions tailored to your household, appliances, and usage patterns.  
How to Use Ecky
Asking Questions  
You can ask Ecky questions such as:  
"What's the cheapest time to run my washing machine today?"
"How does my usage this week compare to last week?"
"When is renewable energy highest this week?"
"Should I run my dishwasher now or wait?"
Getting Personalized Suggestions  
Ecky provides suggestions based on:  
Your registered appliances
Your historical consumption patterns
Current and predicted electricity prices
Current and forecast renewability scores  
Ecky learns from your usage over time and tailors recommendations accordingly.  
How Ecky Works
Access to Scheduled Appliances  
Ecky queries your backend data to identify currently scheduled appliances and their times. Ecky compares each appliance's start and end hours against the current time in German (Europe/Berlin) local time and labels each schedule as:  
Upcoming – The schedule start time has not yet arrived
Running – The appliance is currently within its scheduled time window
Completed – The appliance has finished running within its scheduled time window
Personalization  
Ecky personalizes responses by considering:  
Appliances you have registered
Your typical usage patterns
Your household size
Weather and seasonal factors
Your past interactions and preferences
Limitations  
Ecky's responses are based on the data available and the underlying AI model. While Ecky provides informed suggestions, users should treat responses as helpful guidance rather than absolute truth.  
Common Questions to Ask Ecky
Energy pricing and timing questions
Appliance scheduling questions
Cost and savings estimates
Renewable energy and environmental impact
Usage patterns and comparisons
Household energy efficiency tips

Core Terminology and Glossary  
Category: Reference
Related topics: Dashboard, Recommendations, Scheduler  
Key Definitions
ML Badge  
A small icon shown next to certain features in EcoWat indicating that the feature's output is generated by a machine learning model rather than a direct calculation. The ML badge signals that the output is a prediction or estimate—a helpful suggestion, not a guaranteed fact—and carries some margin of error. Users should treat ML-badged features as informed suggestions rather than guaranteed facts.  
Renewability Score  
An hourly composite percentage (0–100%) representing how much of Germany's current electricity grid generation originates from clean sources (specifically solar and wind). A higher renewability score means greener electricity is available during that hour.  
Day-Ahead Spot Market (EPEX Spot)  
Germany's electricity pricing mechanism where hourly prices are set 24 hours in advance via auction based on projected supply and demand. Prices can go negative when high wind or solar generation coincides with low demand (such as on sunny weekends or windy nights), meaning the grid effectively pays consumers to use electricity during those windows. EcoWat notifies users to consume electricity during these favorable slots.  
Eco Score  
A single combined percentage generated by EcoWat's recommendation algorithm for a given appliance-run time window. The eco score factors in both electricity price and renewable availability. A higher eco score means EcoWat more strongly recommends running the appliance in that time window.  
Timed Appliance  
An appliance that a user has scheduled to run at a specific future time slot, as opposed to running it manually whenever convenient. Timed appliances appear on the Scheduler page.  
Reschedulable vs Non-Reschedulable Appliances  
Reschedulable appliances can realistically be run at different times of day, such as:  
Washing machines
Dishwashers
Electric vehicle (EV) chargers
Heat pumps  
Non-reschedulable appliances must run continuously or at fixed times and are excluded from recommendations. Examples include:  
Refrigerators
Chest freezers
Other always-on appliances
Appliance States  
Every appliance on the dashboard is categorized into one of several states describing its current status:  
Active – The appliance is currently running
Inactive – The appliance is not currently running
High Usage – Consumption during the current session is unusually high
Optimizable – EcoWat's models determine that shifting the appliance's schedule would meaningfully improve cost or renewable-energy alignment  
Appliance states update automatically based on real-time usage data and EcoWat's ongoing analysis.  
Potential Savings  
The projected cost and environmental benefit a user stands to gain by following a specific EcoWat recommendation, compared to running the appliance immediately or at the current time.  
Green Hours  
Time windows when renewable (solar/wind) generation is high and grid carbon intensity is correspondingly low, making them favorable for running high-consumption appliances.

Account Management  
Category: Settings
Related topics: Quick Guide  
Account Registration
Creating an Account  
Registration for EcoWat requires:  
A valid, unique email address (used for login, recovery, and notifications)
A password meeting minimum security requirements:
At least 6 characters long
At least 1 uppercase letter
At least 1 special character (!, @, #, $, %)  
After submitting the registration form, a verification link is emailed to the user. Some features (like appliance scheduling and notifications) remain locked until email verification is complete.  
Email Verification  
A verification link sent via email activates your account. Click the link to unlock scheduling and notification features. If you don't receive the email, check spam folders or request a new verification link.  
Password Management
Minimum Requirements  
EcoWat requires passwords to be at least 6 characters with 1 uppercase letter and 1 special character. However, exceeding the minimum is strongly recommended:  
Use 12+ character passwords (exponentially harder to crack)
Avoid easily guessable information (name, birthday, "password")
Use passphrases (short sentences or unrelated word combinations with special characters/numbers)
Never reuse passwords from other important accounts
Forgotten Password  
If you forget your password:  
Click "Forgot Password" on the login page
Enter your registered email address
Click the reset link sent to your inbox
Create a new password meeting minimum requirements
Log in with your new password
Login Methods  
EcoWat supports two equally secure login methods:  
Magic Link Login
Enter a registered email address
Receive a one-time, secure, time-limited login link (no password needed)
The link is unique, single-use, and expires after roughly 15 minutes
If the link expires, request a new one  
Advantages: More secure than passwords; no password to remember  
Username/Password Login
Standard credential-based login using email and password
Can log in as long as you remember your credentials  
Advantages: Familiar, doesn't require checking email  
Profile and Settings  
The Profile page allows you to:  
View and update your registered email address
Change your password
Review all appliances you have registered with EcoWat
Delete your account (see Account Deletion section)
Account Deletion
Deletion Process  
When you delete your account:  
The account enters a 30-day grace period during which:
Your data is preserved but the account is deactivated
You cannot log in to an active account
During the grace period, logging back in restores full access and cancels deletion
After 30 days without recovery, the account and all data are permanently deleted
Permanent Deletion  
Once 30 days pass without account recovery, deletion is irreversible. The account and all associated data cannot be recovered.  
Data Privacy
Personal Data Confidentiality  
EcoWat is a personal energy-management tool, not a social platform. Your profile details, consumption data, appliances, and predictions are private to you. No other EcoWat user can see your data.  
Data Security  
EcoWat prioritizes the security and privacy of user data at every layer of the platform stack, including encryption, secure authentication, and access controls.

Navigate to the Appliances page
Select an appliance from the supported list
Enter the appliance's typical usage pattern (average daily hours of operation)
Save the appliance  
Once registered, the appliance appears on your Dashboard with its current state and becomes eligible for scheduling recommendations.  
Information Required

Appliance type (from the supported list)
Typical daily operating hours (how many hours per day you typically run this appliance)

StateMeaning
ActiveThe appliance is currently running
InactiveThe appliance is not currently running

Reschedulable vs Non-Reschedulable Appliances
Reschedulable Appliances  
Reschedulable appliances can realistically be run at different times of day and are eligible for scheduling recommendations:  
Washing machines
Dishwashers
Electric vehicle (EV) chargers
Heat pumps

Non-Reschedulable Appliances  
Non-reschedulable appliances must run continuously or at fixed times and are excluded from the Recommendations engine. While you can register them, EcoWat will not generate scheduling recommendations for them:

Managing Appliances

Appliance Prediction Models  
Each supported appliance type has its own tuned prediction model that considers:  
Typical household usage patterns for that appliance
Day of week and seasonal variations
Weather data where relevant
Historical data from similar households  
These individual models enable EcoWat to generate accurate, appliance-specific scheduling recommendations.

Recommendations  
Category: Feature
Related topics: Appliances, Scheduler, Terminology  
What are Recommendations?  
Recommendations are EcoWat's personalized suggestions for when to run your reschedulable appliances to minimize cost and environmental impact. Each recommendation includes:  
The specific appliance to schedule
The optimal time window to run it
Projected cost savings
Environmental benefit (renewable energy alignment)
How Recommendations Work  
EcoWat's recommendation algorithm generates an Eco Score for each possible time window to run an appliance. The Eco Score is a combined percentage (higher is better) that factors in:  
Electricity price: Lower-priced hours (including negative-price hours when the grid pays you to use electricity)
Renewable availability: Hours when the grid's renewable generation is high (high renewability score)  
EcoWat defaults to recommendations that save both money and the environment simultaneously rather than optimizing for one at the expense of the other.  
Potential Savings  
Each recommendation displays projected potential savings showing:  
Cost savings: The estimated reduction in electricity cost if you follow the recommendation
Environmental benefit: The amount of fossil-fuel generation avoided by shifting consumption to greener hours  
Potential savings are calculated by comparing the recommended time window against running the appliance immediately or at the current time.  
Appliances Eligible for Recommendations  
Only reschedulable appliances receive recommendations. The following appliances can be scheduled:  
Washing machines
Dishwashers
Electric vehicle (EV) chargers
Heat pumps  
Non-reschedulable appliances (like refrigerators and freezers) that must run continuously do not receive recommendations.  
Appliance State: Optimizable  
When EcoWat's analysis determines that rescheduling a reschedulable appliance would meaningfully improve cost or renewable-energy alignment, the appliance receives an "Optimizable" state on the Dashboard.  
The optimizable state signals that a strong recommendation exists to shift the appliance's run time.  
Accuracy and Confidence  
Recommendations are powered by machine learning models (indicated by the ML badge). The models carry some margin of error.  
Treat recommendations as informed, data-driven suggestions rather than guaranteed predictions. The underlying models are continuously refined to improve accuracy.

Frequently Asked Questions  
Category: Reference
Related topics: All  
Getting Started  
Q: What devices can I use to access EcoWat?
A: EcoWat is accessible via website on desktop (Windows, macOS, Linux) and native apps on Android and iOS. Both provide identical full functionality. No dedicated Windows or macOS desktop application exists.  
Q: How do I log in to EcoWat?
A: EcoWat supports two login methods. You can use Magic Link (email-based, no password needed) or standard Username/Password login. Both are equally secure.  
Q: I forgot my password. How do I reset it?
A: Click "Forgot Password" on the login page, enter your registered email, and click the reset link sent to your inbox. Create a new password meeting minimum requirements (6+ characters, 1 uppercase, 1 special character).  
Q: What password requirements does EcoWat have?
A: Minimum requirements are: at least 6 characters, at least 1 uppercase letter, and at least 1 special character (!, @, #, $, %). Passwords longer than the minimum (12+ characters) are recommended.  
Q: Can I log in with Google, Apple, or another third-party account?
A: Not currently. EcoWat only supports email/password and magic-link login today. Social and third-party login are planned for a future release.  
Account and Data  
Q: Is my data visible to other EcoWat users?
A: No. EcoWat is a personal energy-management tool, not a social platform. Your profile details, consumption data, appliances, and predictions are private to you.  
Q: What happens to my data if I delete my account?
A: When you delete your account, it enters a 30-day grace period during which your data is preserved but the account is deactivated. If you log back in during this period, the deletion is canceled and your account is restored. After 30 days without recovery, your account and all data are permanently deleted.  
Q: How secure is my data?
A: EcoWat prioritizes security and privacy at every layer of the platform stack, including encryption, secure authentication, and access controls.  
Appliances and Scheduling  
Q: Can I add any appliance I want to EcoWat?
A: Not yet. Only appliances from EcoWat's curated supported list (currently 19 types) can be added. Each appliance requires its own tuned prediction logic and scheduling behavior. The supported list is being actively expanded.  
Q: What is a reschedulable appliance?
A: A reschedulable appliance is one that can realistically be run at different times of day, such as a washing machine or dishwasher. These appliances are eligible for scheduling recommendations.  
Q: What is a non-reschedulable appliance?
A: A non-reschedulable appliance must run continuously or at a fixed time (like a refrigerator or freezer) and cannot be scheduled. These appliances are excluded from recommendations.  
Q: How do I schedule an appliance?
A: Navigate to the Scheduler page, select a reschedulable appliance, choose a start date and time, and confirm. The appliance appears on the Scheduler page and runs at the scheduled time.  
Pricing and Savings  
Q: How does EcoWat help me save money?
A: EcoWat connects to Germany's dynamic Day-Ahead electricity tariffs where power prices fluctuate hourly. By automatically identifying the lowest-cost and negative-price hours and scheduling energy-intensive appliances into those windows, users can achieve significant electricity bill reductions.  
Q: What is Germany's Day-Ahead Spot Market, and why do prices sometimes turn negative?
A: In Germany's EPEX Spot market, electricity prices are set 24 hours in advance via auction. When high wind and strong solar generation coincide with low industrial demand—such as on sunny weekends or windy nights—electricity supply can exceed grid capacity, driving spot market prices negative. The grid effectively pays consumers to use electricity during these windows. EcoWat notifies users to consume electricity during these favorable slots.  
Q: What does "Potential Savings" mean in a recommendation?
A: Potential savings is the projected cost and environmental benefit you stand to gain by following a specific EcoWat recommendation, compared to running the appliance immediately or at the current time.  
Renewable Energy and Environment  
Q: What is the Renewability Score?
A: It's an hourly composite percentage (0–100%) indicating how much of Germany's current power generation originates from clean sources—specifically solar and wind.  
Q: Why should I plan appliance usage around renewable availability, not just price?
A: Using electricity when renewable generation is high means more of the power consumed comes from clean sources, reducing reliance on fossil-fuel generation—even if price alone might suggest a different window.  
Q: Why should I bother saving energy at home?
A: Saving energy lowers electricity bills, reduces demand on the power grid during peak hours, and cuts down greenhouse gas emissions produced by fossil-fuel power plants.  
Q: Does saving a small amount of energy really make a difference?
A: Yes. Small, consistent changes—like running appliances during off-peak hours—add up significantly over time, both financially and environmentally.  
Q: Do small habits, like unplugging chargers, actually help?
A: Yes. Standby power can account for a noticeable share of household electricity use over a year, so unplugging unused devices adds up.  
Q: Can individual household changes really impact the environment?
A: Yes. When many households shift usage toward off-peak and renewable-rich hours, it collectively reduces strain on fossil-fuel power plants and lowers overall emissions.  
Q: What counts as renewable energy?
A: Energy from naturally replenishing sources such as sunlight, wind, and flowing water, as opposed to fossil fuels, which are finite and take millions of years to form.  
Predictions and ML Badges  
Q: How does the 7-day consumption forecast work?
A: The underlying model takes 31 input features—including household size, weather temperatures, day of week, weekend flag, yesterday's total kWh, the 7-day historical average kWh, and planned operating hours for 19 different supported appliance types—to predict daily electricity consumption for each of the next 7 days.  
Q: Is EcoWat always correct?
A: No. Any feature marked with the ML badge is powered by a machine learning model and carries some margin of error. Significant effort goes into tuning these models for strong predictions, but ML-driven outputs should be treated as informed suggestions rather than infallible facts.  
Q: What is the ML badge?
A: The ML badge is a small icon shown next to certain features indicating that the feature's output is generated by a machine learning model rather than a direct calculation. It signals that the output is a prediction or estimate—a helpful suggestion, not a guaranteed fact.  
Technical Questions  
Q: How does Ecky know if my appliance is currently running?
A: Ecky queries today's scheduled appliances from the backend, compares their start and end hours against the current time in German (Europe/Berlin) local time, and labels each schedule as Upcoming, Running, or Completed.  
Q: Are EcoWat's APIs public?
A: Not currently. All API access is scoped to each authenticated user, with no general-purpose public API yet. A public, developer-facing API is planned for a future release.  
Q: What is planned for EcoWat in the future?

Continued refinement of prediction models
Expansion of the supported appliance catalog beyond 19 types

Scheduler  
Category: Feature
Related topics: Appliances, Recommendations, Dashboard  
What is the Scheduler?  
The Scheduler lets you schedule reschedulable appliances to run at specific future time slots. Scheduled appliances appear on the Scheduler page with their start time, end time, and current status (Upcoming, Running, or Completed).  
Scheduling an Appliance
How to Schedule  
To schedule an appliance to run at a specific time:  
Navigate to the Scheduler page
Select a reschedulable appliance
Choose a start date and time
Confirm and save the schedule  
The appliance is now scheduled and appears on the Scheduler page.  
Eligible Appliances  
Only reschedulable appliances can be scheduled. These include:  
Washing machines
Dishwashers
Electric vehicle (EV) chargers
Heat pumps  
Non-reschedulable appliances (like refrigerators) cannot be scheduled because they must run continuously or on fixed schedules.  
Schedule Status  
Every scheduled appliance has a current status indicating its position in the schedule:  
StatusMeaning
UpcomingThe schedule start time has not yet arrived
RunningThe appliance is currently running within its scheduled time window
CompletedThe appliance has finished running within its scheduled time window
Automatic Scheduling Based on Recommendations  
While you can manually schedule any appliance, EcoWat can also suggest optimal schedules based on recommendations. To use EcoWat's suggestions:  
Review recommendations on the Dashboard
Accept a recommended time window
The appliance is automatically scheduled for that window  
Automatic scheduling respects the recommendations' cost and environmental benefits.  
Managing Schedules
Viewing Schedules  
The Scheduler page displays:  
All currently scheduled appliances
Start and end times for each schedule
Current status (Upcoming, Running, Completed)
Historical/completed schedules (optional view)
Editing a Schedule  
To modify a scheduled appliance's time:  
Navigate to the Scheduler page
Select the appliance schedule
Choose a new start time
Confirm the change
Canceling a Schedule  
To cancel a scheduled appliance:  
Navigate to the Scheduler page
Select the appliance schedule
Choose the cancel or delete option
Confirm cancellation  
Once canceled, the appliance no longer appears on the active schedule.  
Time Zone  
EcoWat uses German (Europe/Berlin) local time for all scheduling. All times displayed and scheduled in the app use this time zone.  
Negative Price Hours  
When electricity prices turn negative (the grid pays consumers to use electricity), EcoWat notifies you of these favorable slots. You can schedule high-consumption appliances during negative-price hours to minimize cost.
